t: You're on Gloucester Avenue, a residential street in Primrose Hill, in the London Borough of Camden. It's lined with many nineteenth century properties, including several pubs, and the neo-Georgian Cecil Sharp House. For much of its length it runs alongside the West Coast Main Line out of Euston. The street takes its name from Prince William Frederick, Duke of Gloucester and Edinburgh, a nephew of George III who also became his son-in-law, marrying Princess Mary in 1816.
